marking_verdicts.quantity: addresses held on the coprocessor's I2C buses
marking_verdicts.reason: The port monitors' part of the value rests on the owner's choice: 7 INA3221 on two I²C buses (hardware/STATUS.md:45, 'two I²C buses (owner, 2026-09-25)'; IOBoard.md:351, '4 addresses (0x40 to 0x43) on each'). out_store.c:35-39: STORE_SECTORS is OUT_STORE_SECTORS (2, out_store.h:122) and STORE_RECORDS is FLASH_SECTOR_SIZE / FLASH_PAGE_SIZE, 4,096 / 256 = 16. That gives 32 slots, at 4 MB less 8 kB in the module build. Research.md:102 requires the 2 MB placement. record_t (out_store.c:99-107) is a 20-byte header plus out_store_t, and out_store_t is LINK_OS_COUNT + LINK_CC_COUNT = 8×4 + 8×4 uint16. That makes 148 bytes (link_pages.h:94, :127). Read 2026-09-28 from the checkout.

question_verdicts.reason: This is the P1 asks item of R12 (Research.md:290; categories.json p1_asks R12 'motor temperature register channel'). link_pages.h:229-244 has 1 motor temperature register (5) and :269 has 1 valid bit (bit 4), against the 2 channels of F5 (Research.md:533). IOBoard.md:458 and :483 record it as not stated.

F5's answer (Research.md:533) names a thermocouple and no type. A grep of the checkout at be1f247 for 'thermocouple', 'type K' and 'K-type' finds no type anywhere in the tree. The type sets which front ends apply and the range each measures.

Neither IOBoard.md nor Research.md states a motor temperature range. The tree has only examples: telemetry_sim.c:18 starts at 24.0 °C, and test/host/test_bench.c:29 uses 58.9 °C. The register span (bench_state.c:35-41) is a format limit, not a range the channel must measure.

No accuracy is stated for either channel. The 0.1 °C link step (link_pages.h:235) and the whole-degree display (motor_screen.c:550) are formats, not accuracies. The only ambient range in the sources is the monostable page's 0 to 50 °C. That page calls it 'the range the bench is assumed to be used in' (Monostable.md:27, :318-319 at 23c82ca).

The 20 ms sampling (main.c:1013; IOBoard.md:431) is the firmware loop that samples every bench number. No update rate is stated for the thermocouple channel, and a front end's conversion time is qualified against one.

F15 gives the ESC pack as 67.2 V (Research.md:543). IOBoard.md:443 rates the phase-wire clip for it. No rating is stated for a thermocouple input, although the junction sits on the motor. The value decides whether a front end's input absolute maximum suffices or an isolated input is needed.

No source gives the infrared sensor's position or lead. The length decides sourcing rule 1 (Research.md:134-139) and the signal the lead carries. The question's premise, a sensor off the board, is itself unsourced: see the added question for IOBoard.md:558.
F5 (Research.md:533) gives an infrared channel and no object temperature range. No other line in the tree gives one. A sensor's object range is qualified against it.
No accuracy is stated for the infrared channel on either page or in the tree. A sensor's object-temperature accuracy is qualified against it.

No distance to the motor or target size is stated anywhere in the tree. An infrared sensor's optics variant sets the spot it averages over at that distance. The owner can answer with the full field of view, or with the distance and the spot diameter from which it follows.
The 20 ms bench sampling (IOBoard.md:431) is the firmware loop, not a stated need for the infrared channel. No rate is stated elsewhere.

IOBoard.md:481 records the coprocessor's I²C bus speed as not stated. The one speed setting (settings.c:105-107) belongs to the display's bus. The multiplexer, buffer and extender seeds (Research.md:290) are rated against a clock. The external ports share the coprocessor's buses with the port monitors unless a segment separates them (IOBoard.md:351, :464).
Q7's answer (Research.md:545) gives no cable length or capacitance, and no line in the tree does. The length decides whether a port needs a buffer or a differential extender (seed PCA9615).

A Qwiic port carries its device's 3.3 V supply, and no source states the current. R5 sizes the 3.3 V rail from the parts T2 and T4 select plus the display's draw (Research.md:283), which leaves external devices out.

docs/Manifest.md:14 and :28 put external current sensors on the coprocessor's bus. IOBoard.md:351 and :464 place 0x40 to 0x43 (port monitors) and 0x44 upward (INA238) on both buses. Which addresses an external device needs is not stated. The answer decides whether a port shares a bus or needs its own segment (seed TCA9548A).

The flash store holds 32 slots of 256 bytes (out_store.c:35-39), and today's record is 148 bytes for 8 slots and 8 channels (out_store.c:99-107; link_pages.h:94, :127). out_store.h:64 keeps 'the two pages that describe the outputs, and nothing else'. The record for 20 ports is not defined (IOBoard.md:248). The capacity only feeds Q8 (Research.md:573), so it is decision-only Q8.

IOBoard.md:117 and out_store_map.h:82-84 give what the flash allows: about 3.2 million saves. No source states how many saves the board needs. The value only feeds Q8 (Research.md:573), so it is decision-only Q8.

added.question: Where does the infrared motor temperature sensor sit: off the IO board, on a lead to a connector on the IO board, as IOBoard.md:558 assumes, or on the IO board itself?
added.why: IOBoard.md:558 gives the infrared channel a connector, and no source backs it. F5 (Research.md:533) gives the method and the count only, and Research.md:28 only puts connectors in round 2. The position decides sourcing rule 1: an LCSC number and JLCPCB assembly, or Digi-Key with LCSC number none (Research.md:134-139). It also decides whether the sensor's signal crosses a lead. P1's question 6, the lead's length, rests on this premise.

added.question: Must the thermocouple channel detect an open or unplugged thermocouple, so that the motor temperature valid bit (BENCH flag bit 4) stays clear while none is fitted? Answer yes or no.
added.why: IOBoard.md:432 sets each valid bit 'only when a sensor answered' (link_pages.h:246-276). A thermocouple front end answers on its bus whether or not a thermocouple is plugged in. Holding bit 4 clear with no thermocouple needs the front end to report an open input. P2 checks each front end for open-circuit detection against the answer. It applies to the thermocouple channel if question 0 puts it in the register.

added.question: Over what ambient temperature range (°C, lowest to highest) must the IO board operate, which sets the temperature of the thermocouple's cold junction at its connector?
added.why: The cold junction sits at the IO board's connector (IOBoard.md:558), so the front end's cold-junction error depends on the board's ambient. IOBoard.md and Research.md state no ambient range. The only one in the sources is the monostable page's 0 to 50 °C, given as 'the range the bench is assumed to be used in' (hardware/docs/Monostable.md:27, :318-319 at 23c82ca). That is an assumption. P2 checks each front end's cold-junction accuracy and operating range against the answer.

added.question: What ambient temperature range (°C, lowest to highest) does the infrared sensor itself see at its mounting position near the motor?
added.why: The sensor sits near the motor it measures, so its own temperature is not the IO board's. No source states it. P2 checks each infrared sensor's rated operating range against it, and the object-temperature accuracy its datasheet gives at that ambient.

added.question: Must a device be plugged into or out of an external I2C port while the board is powered, with the bus and the other devices on it still running? Answer yes or no.
added.why: Q7 (Research.md:545) fixes the count, level and connector only. A Qwiic lead plugged into a running bus can disturb transfers on the bus it joins, and the port monitors share the coprocessor's buses (IOBoard.md:351, :464). The answer decides whether a port needs a hot-swap buffer or a segment it can reset alone. P2 checks each buffer, multiplexer or extender (seeds TCA9548A, PCA9615, TCA9617A) against it.
